lines.text: AI helped crack the Riemann hypothesis? Math's biggest puzzle?
That's the claim. An Anthropic mathematician posted it Friday. He says he found it working with Claude.
Unsolved since 1859. There's a million-dollar prize on it.
lines.say: Unsolved since eighteen fifty-nine. There's a million-dollar prize on it.

lines.text: A chatbot did it? Then it doesn't count. I don't trust it.
Fair to wait. It's not peer-reviewed, and he admits he doesn't fully understand it yet.

card.title: CONFIRMED SO FAR
card.body: Released as Lean code, which a computer can check. No human-readable paper yet.

lines.text: Unchecked isn't fake. You rejected it because of who made it.
In 2015, Dietvorst and colleagues found people dropped an algorithm after watching it make mistakes, even when it beat the humans.
lines.say: In twenty fifteen, Dietvorst and colleagues found people dropped an algorithm after watching it make mistakes, even when it beat the humans.

lines.text: So I should just believe the robot?
No. Judge the proof, not the prover. That's what the checks are for.
Does an AI-made proof count? Yes, no, or not until humans get it?
